questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and work of the artist Banksy
How to become a scriptwriter
Why creativity matters for future jobs
Why the BBC is such a good and creative place to work
questions.why: They discuss why creativity is important for future jobs and how we can be more creative.

questions.q: What does the World Economic Forum forecast?
options: Creativity will be a top-three skill for future jobs
Creative industries like music and TV will disappear by 2020
Young people will find jobs more easily
Most jobs will be in art and music
questions.why: It forecasts that by 2020 creativity will be in the top three most important skills for future jobs.

questions.q: According to Bernadette Duffy, what is the problem with how schools teach?
options: They teach too much art
They don't teach important subjects like maths and reading
Teachers have too little time
They teach skills in ways that are easy to measure
questions.why: She says we teach important things 'in a way that makes them easier to measure'.

questions.q: What does Bernadette Duffy want schools to focus on more?
options: Gaining more skills
Using skills in a creative way
Passing more tests
Learning about computers
questions.why: She wants less focus purely on gaining skills and 'far far more on actually using them in a creative way'.

questions.q: Why does Rob mention one of the BBC's values?
options: To show his organisation sees creativity as essential
To complain about his job
To explain how the BBC trains its new staff to be creative
To advertise a new programme
questions.why: He says the value states that 'creativity is the lifeblood of our organisation'.

questions.q: What does Nick Skillicorn suggest everyone should do each day?
options: Work at a desk for longer
Read a book for an hour before starting work
Take 15 minutes of unfocused time
Write down all their ideas
questions.why: He says everyone should take fifteen minutes of unfocused time, not looking at any screen.

questions.q: Where does Rob say he gets his headspace?
options: At his desk in the office
Watching TV
Talking to colleagues
In the bath or riding his bike
questions.why: Rob says he has headspace when lying in the bath or out riding his bike.

questions.q: Why does Neil say creativity will be vital for children starting school now?
options: Because they will be too busy with technology to learn
They may do jobs that don't exist yet
Because schools are closing
Because art is more popular than ever
questions.why: He says they will grow up to do a job that doesn't yet exist, facing challenges like AI.
